source_refs.note: Topic 7.2 as printed (PDF 94-95, printed 90-91): the Class Activity, null and alternative hypotheses, the Example box and Formulating correct hypotheses.

blocks.text: Hypotheses are classified into different types. Each type has a specific purpose. The most common types are null and alternative hypotheses. These types work together in testing. Correct hypotheses improve analysis quality by reducing confusion. They guide decision-making. Understanding hypothesis types is important. They form the base of hypothesis testing.

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Students write a null and alternative hypothesis for marks or percentage situation. Discuss correctness.

The null hypothesis states that there is no effect or difference. It is written as a default assumption. Data is tested against this hypothesis. If evidence is strong, the null hypothesis is rejected. It is usually represented by H₀. The null hypothesis helps avoid bias. It provides a comparison base. Many tests start with this hypothesis. It is important in decision-making.

The alternative hypothesis states that there is an effect or difference. It is written as opposite of the null hypothesis. It is represented by H₁ or Ha. The goal of testing is often to support this hypothesis. Evidence must be strong to accept it. It represents change or impact. Alternative hypotheses guide research direction. They explain expected outcomes. Testing compares both hypotheses.
Research Question: Does the amount of study time affect students' exam scores?
H₀ (Null Hypothesis): There is no significant relationship between study time and exam scores.
H₁ (Alternative Hypothesis): The amount of study time significantly affects students' exam scores.

Correct hypotheses must be clear and specific. They should be testable using data. Vague statements reduce accuracy. Hypotheses must match research questions. Variables should be defined clearly. Simple language improves understanding. Correct formulation saves time. It leads to reliable results. Proper hypotheses improve analysis quality.
